dimensions.note: Unchanged: the token is sensitive in the schema and api.ts masks a token the forge echoes back. names.ts logs only data names, never a token or a mirror credential.

Every method logs on entry and completion with structured placeholders. writeRecord logs once per record, at warning, the first time a portable name is written while the pre-2026.11.09.1 name holds data, with {legacy} and {name} as properties, and points at the README for the removal. Verified live against Forgejo 17.0.1: one notice per old record on the first run, none on the second, none for org and user whose names did not change.

Unchanged for every HTTP path: call() throws with method, path, status and the forge's message. readOrNull swallows every error from readResource deliberately: the read-back only decides whether to print the notice, and a name Windows cannot store fails at the path rather than as not-found; the write itself still surfaces its own errors. work_item_sync's fallback read of the old link name goes through the same readOrNull.

names_test.ts covers slug, dataName, repoName, both legacy transforms and writeRecord (one notice, never twice; quiet without old data, with an unchanged name, without readResource and when the old name cannot be read). push_mirror_test covers the attribute-based stale check, including an owner whose login is a prefix of another's and an old-named record left alone. 123 tests. Still open from earlier releases: the base's 23 upstream methods are tested through their helpers and a mocked fetch, not through execute with a fake context, so the renamed write sites in forgejo.ts are proven by type checking and the live run (repo_ensure, repo_list, org_ensure, repo_topics_ensure, label_ensure, push_mirror_list) rather than by a unit test each.

Unchanged for every method. The name change is non-destructive: nothing deletes, renames or rewrites data under an old name, and push_mirror_list's reconciliation skips any name containing ':' so an old pushMirror record is never dropped as stale. work_item_sync reads its link under the new name and then the old one, so a work item mirrored before the change is updated rather than filed again.

Unchanged: no request or response handling changed. push_mirror_list now reads its own stored records through context.readModelData with the behavior's definition name, the documented cross-behavior read, instead of walking the data repository.
Unchanged: fetch timeouts are cleared in finally in the shared caller; no files or handles. The two read-backs in writeRecord run concurrently and hold nothing.
Tests and README use acme, tool, example-org and forge.example.com; the issue links point at the public tracker and the Swamp Club lab.
Unchanged: no passthrough anywhere; the objects written are the schema types themselves, so schema-write conformance is as before at every renamed site (the data argument of each write is untouched).

Unchanged: every spec infinite except userMatch at 7d; the README now says so in one place. An item left under an old name is never expired by GC, which is why the README gives the explicit prefix delete.

Enumerated in the README's table, 30 specs: status; <org>; <login>; and for everything about a repository a spec word first, then owner, repo and any further part, joined with '-', each part through slug ([A-Za-z0-9._-], trailing dots trimmed): repo-, mirror-, webhook-, collaborator-, branch-protection-, pull-, actions-secret-, runner-registration-, runner-, runner-prune-, repo-rename-, push-mirror-, push-mirror-delete-, pull-mirror-, repo-topics-, repo-units-, pr-assignment-, user-match-, repo-delete-, org-delete-, issue-, issue-labels-, label-, pr-feedback-, pr-comment-, pr-merge-state-, work-item-. The shape is @dataverket/github's repo-<repo> kept from upstream; the owner stays because one model spans every org. No ':' anywhere (dataverket-org/swamp-extensions#1, swamp-club/swamp#3205); verified live that swamp's portability warning is gone. Accepted, as upstream accepts for release-a-b-c: parts carry '-', so acme/corp-x and acme-corp/x share a name within a spec, and a crafted owner login equal to a spec word (an owner named 'delete') could make repo-<owner>-<repo> meet repo-delete-<owner>-<repo>; the attributes say which record it is, and the only reconciliation that deletes, push_mirror_list's, goes by attributes. Pre-existing and kept: a repository literally named 'org' shares label names with the organization's labels.

writeRecord reads back the latest record under the new and the old name through context.readResource, both tolerant of failure, only to decide whether to print the one-time notice. push_mirror_list reads its own pushMirror records through readModelData and filters by the owner and repo attributes. work_item_sync reads its previous link under the new name and falls back to the old one. All documented context API; nothing renames, and the only delete is the pre-existing drop of a vanished mirror's record under a portable name. Old data is left in place; the README documents its removal with swamp data delete --prefix per owner plus 'user:', dry run first, verified live to leave the org record alone.

Version 2026.11.09.1 with a no-op upgrades entry after 2026.10.26.1; the global arguments are unchanged, so a definition is stamped and not transformed. forgejo_test.ts checks the chain ends at the model's version. Verified live: an instance created at 2026.10.27.1 reports typeVersion 2026.11.09.1 and staleness current after one run.
